070.note: Housing/Meals/Pay must be an EXPLICIT host decision before publication (founder, 2026-07-17). A column default must be the WEAKEST claim, not the strongest. Adds listings_publication_triad_chk: a non-sourced listing may not enter under_review/live while any of the three evidences is 'not_stated' — enforced in the DB because that is the only layer on EVERY writer's path (Supabase's default table grants give `authenticated` full-column UPDATE on listings, so a server-action-only gate is decorative). Sourced listings keep 'not_stated' (founder decision 4) via the provenance escape hatch. Free and backfill-less ONLY because production has 0 listings. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge — never applied by agents.

071.note: Closes the escape hatch under 070's publication gate. LIVE-VERIFIED: `authenticated` holds a TABLE-level UPDATE grant on public.listings (all 67 columns) — no migration ever locked it down, unlike 050 (messages/conversations), 054 (host_profiles) and 061 (seeker_profiles). So a host could PATCH provenance='sourced' + status='live' in ONE PostgREST request and walk straight through listings_publication_triad_chk's sourced exemption, publishing a listing with no answered benefits. Revokes the blanket grant and re-grants UPDATE on exactly the columns host code writes (the 21 in ListingColumnPatch + benefit_details + status). Excludes provenance/source_*/claim_summary/host_profile_id/completion_score/accepted_count — none of which any host path writes. published_at/paused_at/archived_at move to a BEFORE UPDATE trigger instead of being granted (the 067 precedent: 'trigger assignment — no column grant needed, the lockdown stays intact'), which also stops a host forging published_at to game feed ordering. Service-role paths (admin, moderation, sourced ingestion, expiry sweep) bypass grants entirely and are unaffected. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge.

079.note: Makes the account-deletion confirmation TRUE. HostSettings opened a mailto: and then unconditionally rendered 'Deletion request received. Our team will process it within 5 business days and confirm via email.' — nothing was stored, so a person with no configured mail client (or who closed the compose window) was told their request had been received when nobody had received anything, and the platform held no evidence an erasure request ever arrived. That evidence is exactly what a statutory clock is measured against (GDPR Art. 17, CCPA/CPRA). Adds account_deletion_requests (scope host|seeker, denormalized display_label so the operator queue can still identify an account whose profile is gone, open/in_progress/completed/rejected/withdrawn, requester + resolution notes), a partial unique index giving ONE open request per user per scope (a second click must not duplicate the queue), owner-only SELECT/INSERT RLS with UPDATE/DELETE revoked from authenticated so a requester can never mark their own erasure complete, and an updated_at trigger. Deliberately records the REQUEST rather than deleting: a host may have live listings, in-flight applications or payment obligations, so erasure stays a reviewed operation. The '5 business days' commitment was removed from the UI in the same change because no operator process backs it. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge — never applied by agents.

080.note: Closes the host_profiles column exposure created by 072. 027 revoked table-wide SELECT from anon and re-granted a public-safe list; 072 then revoked table-wide SELECT from `authenticated` but re-granted EVERY column except benefit_library via a dynamic pg_attribute loop — so a signed-in seeker could read STRICTLY MORE than an anonymous visitor on any host with a live listing (policy 013:132 is to anon+authenticated, and the anon key ships in the client bundle). Exposed: primary_latitude/primary_longitude (exact coordinates), trust_status ('internal only' per 003), account_status + removed_at/reason_code/by_user_id/notes (enforcement history), flagged_for_review/reason/at (054 spam flags), public_status, attestation internals, completion_score, operating_regions, slug, logo/cover_asset_id, owner_user_id. Revokes exactly those 21 columns from anon AND authenticated. Every one was verified to have ZERO readers through the anon/authenticated roles — the only readers are service-role (admin, moderation, notifications), which bypass column grants — so this needs NO application change and cannot 403 a live query. Existence-guarded per column so a reset/rename is a no-op. DEFERRED to a separate change: clerk_user_id and deleted_at, which authenticated genuinely reads today (self-application guard + invite-accept email read ANOTHER host's clerk_user_id; owner queries FILTER on both, and a WHERE-only reference still needs SELECT). Removing those means routing ~11 call sites through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs whose failure mode is a runtime 403 — individually verified, not bundled. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge — never applied by agents.

081.note: The prerequisite 080's deferral note did not know it needed. 080 scoped the clerk_user_id/deleted_at follow-up as '~11 call sites' — a count derived from code that NAMES the column, and therefore incomplete. It missed RLS policies on OTHER tables whose USING/WITH CHECK sub-selects host_profiles. 080:15 is right that a policy on host_profiles itself is evaluated as the table owner; that does NOT extend to a cross-table sub-select, which becomes an ordinary range-table entry permission-checked against the INVOKING role, column bitmap included. Verified empirically (role authenticated, real column grants, local DB): sub-select on an ungranted column of a second table raises 42501; same shape with the column granted returns the row; an OR branch that would have matched does NOT short-circuit the check on the other branch; routing through a SECURITY DEFINER helper is allowed. Eleven live policies were in the inline shape — host_announcements owner_read_all/owner_insert/owner_update, and storage.objects listing_media and profile_photos select/insert/update/delete_own_folder — contributed by four migrations (017, 023, 031, 072) and enumerated from pg_policy on a database rebuilt through 080, not by grepping migrations. Had the revoke landed alone it would have 42501'd every listing-media upload, every profile photo upload INCLUDING SEEKERS (the OR result above: the profile_photos policies are host-branch OR seeker-branch, and a seeker with no host_profiles row still fails on a host_profiles column), and the whole host_announcements community feed for every signed-in user — none of it host_profiles code, and none of it visible to a smoke test, because public image delivery bypasses storage RLS via /storage/v1/object/public/. Rewrites all eleven onto current_host_profile_ids()/current_seeker_profile_ids(), which is already the house pattern behind listings_select_own, conversations_select_party, host_attestations_all_own, team_memberships_all_host and invites_select_party — the eleven were the inconsistent ones. Semantics unchanged (the helper is the same predicate, additionally gating the Clerk sub on its format); 072's Housing-evidence carve-out reproduced verbatim. REVOKES NOTHING — it only removes dependencies, so it is safe to apply alone and safe to leave applied if the revoke is deferred. Ends with a DO block that fails the migration if any anon/authenticated policy still sub-selects host_profiles.clerk_user_id. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge — never applied by agents.

Adds a SECURITY DEFINER RPC returning exactly the applicant fields a host may see, and only for seekers who have actually applied to or been invited by that host - never a general seeker directory. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge.

085.note: Founder decisions 2026-07-26. (1) No free tier: a host may not create a profile or publish without an active paid subscription, so subscription state must be resolvable independently of host_profiles (today subscription_tier is a column ON host_profiles, which cannot gate the creation of the row that carries it). (2) Team seats and the basic/full analytics split are INCLUDED per tier, not add-on products - they need real code paths rather than being zeroed out. (3) Additional listings are a paid add-on priced by tier, which needs a per-host purchased-allowance column so the cap check can count it. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge.

086.note: Commercial redesign phase 2, decision D6 (PRE-BILLING HOST MODE). Moves the PAID line from profile creation to PUBLICATION. 083 refused create_my_host_profile without an active paid tier, which made an unpaid account and a host workspace the same thing and put the price in front of a host who had not yet seen the product. This redefines that function with the paid-tier refusal REMOVED and every other check kept verbatim: identity, company name presence and length, primary location length, category scope cardinality and membership, scope de-duplication, the soft-delete refusal, the existing-profile early return and its denormalized-tier reconcile, the slug retry loop and its conflict handling. Grants are unchanged. Nothing about the PUBLICATION gate moves: private.enforce_listing_allowance still counts live plus paused plus under_review against private.plan_listing_allowance, which is 0 for tier none, so a host with no plan may hold unlimited drafts and may not put a single listing in front of a seeker. That was already true before this migration - tier none was already an allowance of 0 - so this is a one-gate change, and the publication refusal is pinned by tests rather than assumed. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge.

087.note: Commercial redesign phase 4, decision D10 (FOUNDING HOST PROGRAM). The program was a term sheet with no code path: contracts carried the locked rates and a seat cap, six dormant Stripe prices existed, and nothing counted a claim, so guardrail G53 forbade the words outright. This makes it real and keeps it DARK until the founder configures it. public.founding_host_program is a singleton row (id = 1) carrying capacity, claimed, enrollment_deadline and status draft|open|full|ended; anon and authenticated hold SELECT on exactly those four columns so a public surface can render REAL numbers and nothing else, and no client role holds any write. public.founding_host_claims records one claim per Clerk identity (unique), invisible to every client role. public.claim_founding_host_seat(text) is the only way a seat is consumed: SECURITY DEFINER, service_role EXECUTE only, per-program advisory lock, and it increments claimed ONLY while status is open, the deadline is in the future and claimed is below capacity, flipping status to full on the last seat. It is idempotent per Clerk id, so a redelivered Stripe webhook cannot consume two seats. public.founding_host_claim_discrepancies plus public.record_founding_claim_discrepancy(text, text, text) exist for the race the money creates: a checkout that opened while the program was open can be paid after it filled, and the honest answer is to grant the paid tier and record the over-subscription where the founder can see it, never to over-claim capacity. Additive/idempotent; apply via db-migrate pipeline on merge.

088.note: Application-scoped interview scheduling: participant-only requests/options, JWT-derived mutation RPCs, canonical scheduling lifecycle enforcement, and no provider or realtime activation. Additive; apply only through the reviewed db-migrate pipeline after merge.

Grants only UPDATE(remote_preference), preserves row-level owner policies and every server-authoritative column exclusion, and never applies outside the reviewed db-migrate pipeline.

090.note: Makes every future message and its canonical message_sent event one PostgreSQL transaction. An AFTER INSERT trigger validates sender-to-conversation identity and writes routing-only outbox metadata for all writers; authenticated callers lose direct INSERT and use a Clerk-JWT-derived RPC that preserves existing thread semantics and the 4,000-character body bound. Additive/idempotent; apply only through the reviewed db-migrate pipeline after merge.

091.note: Makes application submission and invite acceptance one JWT-derived database transaction, with authoritative resume, listing, expiry, attribution, deduplication, and reactivation enforcement. Reviewed pipeline only; not applied by agents.

092.note: Makes listing cover/gallery ownership authoritative for authenticated Data API writes: exact deployment origin, listing-media bucket, owning host UUID prefix, safe child path, and an existing Storage object. Ordinary legacy rows fail closed on their next edit; converted claim rows preserve byte-identical inherited source media while snapshotting and restoring it across conversion/revocation. Reviewed pipeline only; not applied by agents.
